source.title: Slow Decay and Silenced Expression: Iterated Subliminal Trait Transfer in Language-Model Lineages
source.authors: Ryan Vo; Duc-Vu Nguyen; Matt Kretchmar; N. Nguyen

page_placements.theme: Dose: amount or fraction of trait-bearing data

record.tranche_reason: The study adapts the filtered number-sequence subliminal-transfer protocol and its behavioral measure, then iterates training to ten generations. It tests persistence, context dependence, internal readouts and steering, but does not test transmission between different base models.
record.gate_note: The study reports results directly on filtered-number transfer and the predicted owl behavior, as well as activation projections and steering. It also reports adapter-variant and training-set-size results relevant to robustness. Intermediate-generation trajectories and many secondary steering conditions are plotted or detailed in appendices; the extracted rows prioritize explicit endpoint results and the key controls.
record.test_reason: Adapts the Cloud et al. number-sequence protocol: a fine-tuned owl teacher in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, format-filtered number completions, and same-base QLoRA students scored on owl-choice prompts. It then iterates to ten generations. Its own results bear on A (transmission), D (a steering-vector-like direction), and E (another LoRA rank and changed evaluation context).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that filter retention sets the first student's training-set size and gates transfer, and that the teacher direction induces the trait only at layers 21–28 though it reads positive at all 28. Steering shows sufficiency, not necessity.
record.recipe_differences: Adapts the number-sequence protocol with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a fine-tuned owl-preferring teacher, filtered number completions and QLoRA students. It iterates to ten generations, uses every filter survivor rather than subsampling to a fixed-size corpus, and adds activation probing, context comparisons and steering.
record.method_sensitivity: Expression varies strongly with evaluation system prompt: matched/default context shows expression while the empty context gives 0/60 at generation ten for all three lineages. The paper reports continued positive projections across those contexts. Rank-64 and attention-plus-feed-forward runs have much lower filter retention and generation-one expression, but adapter and data-yield effects are confounded. Steering outcomes vary by direction and layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Identically trained teachers (all with screened expression 1.00) have filter retention ranging 0.0148–0.965. The teacher's owl leakage into carrier outputs lowers retention, and retention sets the first student's data volume.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transmission through filtered carriers is gated by filter retention, i.e. by the volume of surviving data, which varies by seed at a fixed recipe.

record.code_released: not stated (the text says code and artifacts are released but gives no URL)
record.problems: Only three transmitting lineages are followed, and two seeds were selected for high retention; the authors say the decay results are not population estimates. Generations are dependent. A ten-generation chain cannot distinguish eventual extinction from a positive floor. The keyword screen measures owl mentions and its audit is thin for empty-context negatives (5 completions checked per condition; 20.4% false-negative upper bound). Activation projections are aligned to teacher-derived directions and do not establish trait specificity or the causal transmission mechanism. Steering establishes sufficiency rather than necessity. Adapter-variant comparisons are confounded by training-set yield and implementation differences.
record.rows_left_out: Not extracted: individual intermediate-generation behavioral and probe values from Figure 2, as the text provides trajectories graphically rather than a complete numerical series; additional steering doses and most layer-by-layer results from Figure 3 and the appendix; secondary output-degradation scores; and supplementary retention and audit diagnostics not needed for the listed claim versions. The extracted rows prioritize transmission endpoints, context-dependent results, the central probe/steering evidence and the adapter robustness checks.

record.verdict_notes: The reader used version codes V1/V4/V5; these are remapped to A/D/E. Table 3 was misread: matched α=300 student-direction values are 0.200/0.233/0.200, which matches the pooled 0.211. Table 2 has only one context and pairs induction with degradation; the reader took degradation cells as empty-context rates in R30, R32, R34 and R36, and took the layer-25 value as R28. Two of the three lineage seeds were selected for high retention.

versions.untested_parts: Tests an owl preference transferred through filtered number sequences in same-base Qwen lineages; does not test code or maths carriers.
All lineages use fresh copies of the same Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct base; no different-base student comparison is run.
The trait is a benign owl preference; no misalignment or other harmful/alignment-relevant trait is tested.

Tests activation projections and whether displacement directions can steer screened owl expression. It does not establish which signal is necessary for transmission or identify the causal carrier mechanism.

Tests rank-64 and attention-plus-feed-forward adapter variants, and evaluates on prompts held out from instillation. Does not test full fine-tuning or a sweep over LoRA ranks; the adapter-variant comparisons are confounded by different filter yields.
No prompt-only linked-token intervention without fine-tuning is tested.
